description: Move the denormalised click counters off the 'links' table into a new 'link_counters' table keyed by link_id, so the rollup writes a table nothing latency-sensitive reads. This is one coherent change spanning the Drizzle schema, a new migration (0009), the worker rollup, the redirect resolver, all API readers, and the DB tests. Implements architecture epic #267 Phase 1 / issue #270, recommendation (a). Depends on FEAT-001 (green baseline).
steps: FOLLOW-UP (missed reader): apps/worker/src/jobs/outbox.ts sweepExpired() reads `l.clicks >= l.click_limit` from the links table (~line 112). This is a SCHEDULED worker job (called from apps/worker/src/main.ts:69) and will throw at runtime once migration 0009 drops links.clicks. Repoint it at link_counters: LEFT JOIN link_counters lc ON lc.link_id = l.id and change the predicate to `coalesce(lc.clicks, 0) >= l.click_limit`, preserving the exact expired-by-click-limit semantics. This is the same click-limit gate logic the resolver/gateFor and the API list status filters use, so it must read the same source.

DONE. SCHEMA (packages/database/src/schema/links.ts): Add a new pgTable 'link_counters' with columns: linkId uuid('link_id').primaryKey().references(() => links.id, { onDelete: 'cascade' }); clicks integer('clicks').notNull().default(0); uniqueClicks integer('unique_clicks').notNull().default(0). Mirror the exact column names/types/semantics the two columns currently have on links (see the 'Denormalised counters' block, ~lines 112-121). Remove the 'clicks' and 'uniqueClicks' fields from the 'links' pgTable definition (delete those two lines and, if desired, the now-stale part of the comment). Add a 'linkCountersRelations' (one link_counters -> one links via linkId) and add a matching relation on linksRelations if the file's relation style calls for it (keep it consistent with existing relations; a one() back-reference is optional but the FK relation should be declared so drizzle-kit sees the reference). Ensure link_counters is exported (schema/index.ts re-exports './links.js' with export *, so a new export const is picked up automatically).

MIGRATION (packages/database/drizzle/0009_link_counters.sql): Hand-write SQL following the 0008 header-comment + statement-breakpoint style. Statements, in order: (1) CREATE TABLE "link_counters" ( "link_id" uuid PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL, "clicks" integer DEFAULT 0 NOT NULL, "unique_clicks" integer DEFAULT 0 NOT NULL ); (2) INSERT INTO "link_counters" ("link_id", "clicks", "unique_clicks") SELECT "id", "clicks", "unique_clicks" FROM "links"; -- backfill so any populated dev/fixture DB stays consistent (pre-deployment, so trivially correct); (3) ALTER TABLE "link_counters" ADD CONSTRAINT "link_counters_link_id_links_id_fk" FOREIGN KEY ("link_id") REFERENCES "public"."links"("id") ON DELETE cascade ON UPDATE no action; (4) ALTER TABLE "links" DROP COLUMN "clicks"; (5) ALTER TABLE "links" DROP COLUMN "unique_clicks". Use the exact drizzle-generated constraint/PK naming conventions (compare to 0008 which named the FK 'click_daily_uniques_link_id_links_id_fk' and PK 'click_daily_uniques_link_id_day_pk'; here the PK is on link_id so drizzle names it 'link_counters_link_id_pk' if declared as a table-level pk, but since link_id is a column-level .primaryKey() drizzle emits it inline as 'PRIMARY KEY' with no separate constraint - match whatever drizzle-kit generate actually produces). Separate statements with the '--> statement-breakpoint' marker exactly as other migrations do.

MIGRATION META: Add a journal entry idx 9 for tag '0009_link_counters' to packages/database/drizzle/meta/_journal.json (copy the shape of the idx 8 entry; use a 'when' timestamp greater than 0008's 1788029831657). Create packages/database/drizzle/meta/0009_snapshot.json. STRONGLY PREFERRED: instead of hand-writing the snapshot, run 'pnpm --filter @snapurl/database generate' AFTER editing the schema so drizzle-kit produces the migration SQL, snapshot, and journal entry for you; then hand-edit ONLY the generated .sql to insert the backfill INSERT statement (step 2 above) between the CREATE TABLE and the DROP COLUMNs. If drizzle-kit names the migration file something other than 0009_link_counters.sql, that generated name is fine - keep drizzle's name and journal tag in sync. The end state MUST be: 'drizzle-kit generate' reports NO further drift (the schema and the 0009 snapshot agree).

WORKER ROLLUP (apps/worker/src/jobs/rollup.ts): Replace the final 'update links l set clicks=..., unique_clicks=...' statement (the block under the 'The denormalised counters on links' comment) with an UPSERT into link_counters keyed on link_id. Keep the existing aggregation from click_daily (recompute-not-increment) unchanged; only change the write target. Use: INSERT INTO link_counters (link_id, clicks, unique_clicks) SELECT link_id, sum(clicks)::int, sum(uniques)::int FROM click_daily WHERE link_id IN (select distinct link_id from rollup_batch) GROUP BY link_id ON CONFLICT (link_id) DO UPDATE SET clicks = excluded.clicks, unique_clicks = excluded.unique_clicks. Update the surrounding comment to say the counter now lives in link_counters (still recomputed, still what the click-limit gate reads, still can overshoot). Confirm NO other statement in this file (or any scheduled job in apps/worker) issues an UPDATE against links.

REDIRECT RESOLVER (apps/redirect/src/resolver.ts): The ResolvedLink interface (lines ~18-46, including 'clicks: number' at ~line 29) MUST remain byte-for-byte unchanged. In PostgresLinkResolver.resolve(), the main query currently does select({ link: links, domainId: domains.id }).from(links).innerJoin(domains, ...). Add a LEFT JOIN to link_counters on eq(linkCounters.linkId, links.id) and select the counter's clicks, coalescing to 0 when no counter row exists yet: e.g. select({ link: links, domainId: domains.id, clicks: sql<number>`coalesce(${linkCounters.clicks}, 0)` }). Then set clicks: row.clicks (from the joined/coalesced value) instead of row.link.clicks at ~line 106. This keeps the read a cheap indexed PK lookup on link_counters (no N+1). Import linkCounters from '@snapurl/database'.

REDIRECT gateFor (apps/redirect/src/main.ts): No functional change - gateFor reads link.clicks which is still populated (now from link_counters). Confirm it compiles and the click-limit logic at ~line 176 is untouched.

API links.mapper.ts (apps/api/src/links/links.mapper.ts): LinkRow currently declares clicks/uniqueClicks and toLinkDto reads row.clicks / row.uniqueClicks / deriveStatus({...clicks}). The external Link DTO MUST keep clicks and uniqueClicks. Keep LinkRow.clicks and LinkRow.uniqueClicks as fields (they will be populated by the service query from link_counters, coalesced to 0). Do NOT remove them from the DTO.

API links.service.ts (apps/api/src/links/links.service.ts): (a) In list() and get(), the query does select({ link: links, domain: domains.domain, creator: users.name }). Because links no longer has clicks/unique_clicks, add a LEFT JOIN link_counters (on eq(linkCounters.linkId, links.id)) and select the two counter values coalesced to 0, then merge them into the LinkRow passed to hydrate/toLinkDto. Concretely: extend the select to include clicks: sql<number>`coalesce(${linkCounters.clicks}, 0)` and uniqueClicks: sql<number>`coalesce(${linkCounters.uniqueClicks}, 0)`, then when building the LinkRow ({ ...r, link: r.link as LinkRow }) spread these two values onto the link object so LinkRow.clicks/uniqueClicks are set (e.g. link: { ...r.link, clicks: r.clicks, uniqueClicks: r.uniqueClicks } as LinkRow). Do the same in both list() (paged rows query AND keep the count query working - the count query does not select link columns so it only needs the join added if a filter references link_counters) and get(). (b) The raw-SQL status filters in list() reference ${links.clicks} in four places (notExpired, the 'expired' branch, the 'active' branch). Those columns no longer exist on links. Replace ${links.clicks} in those raw sql fragments with a coalesced reference to the counter, and add the LEFT JOIN link_counters to the total-count query and the paged query so the reference resolves. Use coalesce(${linkCounters.clicks}, 0) in place of ${links.clicks} everywhere it appears in these filters, preserving the exact comparison semantics (>=, <). (c) exportCsv pages through list() and reads link.clicks / link.uniqueClicks off the DTO - unchanged once list() populates them. Keep changes surgical; do not refactor unrelated code.

API conversions.service.ts (apps/api/src/conversions/conversions.service.ts): The byLink query selects clicks: links.clicks and groupBy(..., links.clicks). Change the select to clicks: sql<number>`coalesce(${linkCounters.clicks}, 0)` and add a LEFT JOIN link_counters on eq(linkCounters.linkId, links.id); update the groupBy to group by the counter column (linkCounters.clicks) or by linkCounters.linkId instead of links.clicks. Preserve the cvr / percentChange math which reads r.clicks. Import linkCounters.

DB TEST rollup.test.ts (apps/worker/src/jobs/rollup.test.ts): The test 'writes the denormalised counters on links from the rollups' does `select clicks, unique_clicks from links where id = ${linkId}`. Change it to `select clicks, unique_clicks from link_counters where link_id = ${linkId}` (keep the assertions row.clicks === rolled.clicks and row.unique_clicks === rolled.uniques). Verify no other query in this file reads links.clicks/unique_clicks.

DB TEST links.service.integration.test.ts (apps/api/src/links/links.service.integration.test.ts): addLink() inserts clicks on the links table (opts.clicks ?? 0). Since links no longer has a clicks column, remove clicks from the links insert .values({...}) and instead, after inserting the link (and it returns id), insert a link_counters row for that link when opts.clicks is provided (or always, defaulting to 0): db.insert(linkCounters).values({ linkId: row.id, clicks: opts.clicks ?? 0 }). Import linkCounters from '@snapurl/database'. This keeps the 'limited' fixture (clickLimit 10, clicks 10) driving the expired-by-click-limit status assertions. Confirm the status filters (which now read link_counters via the service join) still classify the seeded fixtures the same way.

CONTRACT check (packages/contract): grep for clicks/uniqueClicks in packages/contract; confirm the Link type still declares clicks and uniqueClicks and DO NOT change it (the API still returns them). web/src/lib/api/fixtures.ts is frontend fixture data and stays unchanged.
Run 'pnpm --filter @snapurl/database generate' one final time and confirm it reports NO drift (no new migration wanted). If it wants to emit one, reconcile the schema/migration until it is clean.
acceptance_criteria: A new 'link_counters' table exists in the schema with link_id (PK, FK to links ON DELETE CASCADE), clicks (int not null default 0), unique_clicks (int not null default 0).
The 'links' table no longer declares clicks or unique_clicks (schema) and migration 0009 drops both columns after backfilling link_counters.
apps/worker/src/jobs/rollup.ts writes counters via INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (link_id) DO UPDATE into link_counters; NO scheduled job issues an UPDATE against links.
apps/redirect/src/resolver.ts ResolvedLink interface is byte-for-byte unchanged; resolve() sources clicks from link_counters via LEFT JOIN coalesced to 0.
gateFor in apps/redirect/src/main.ts still enforces the click limit reading link.clicks.

All API readers of the two columns (links.service list/get/exportCsv status filters, conversions.service byLink) source clicks/uniqueClicks from link_counters; the external Link DTO still exposes clicks and uniqueClicks.
rollup.test.ts and links.service.integration.test.ts read/seed link_counters instead of links.clicks/unique_clicks.
pnpm type-check passes; NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL=... pnpm build passes; pnpm test passes locally (DB-gated suites skipped).
verification: pnpm --filter @snapurl/database generate (confirm it reports no schema drift / does not want a new migration)

grep -rn 'links.clicks\|links.uniqueClicks\|unique_clicks from links\|update links' apps packages | review: confirm no remaining reader of links.clicks/unique_clicks and no UPDATE against links in scheduled jobs
findings: Implemented recommendation (a). Changes: (1) packages/database/src/schema/links.ts - added `linkCounters` pgTable (link_id uuid PK -> links.id ON DELETE cascade, clicks int not null default 0, unique_clicks int not null default 0), removed clicks/uniqueClicks from `links`, added linkCountersRelations + a `counters` one() back-reference on linksRelations. (2) Migration: ran `pnpm --filter @snapurl/database generate` after the schema edit; drizzle emitted drizzle/0009_third_kang.sql plus meta/0009_snapshot.json and the idx-9 journal entry. Hand-added the header comment and the backfill `INSERT INTO link_counters SELECT id, clicks, unique_clicks FROM links` between CREATE TABLE and the FK/DROP COLUMN statements (runs while links still has the columns). Final `generate` reports NO drift. (3) apps/worker/src/jobs/rollup.ts - final `update links` replaced with `insert into link_counters ... select ... from click_daily ... group by link_id on conflict (link_id) do update set clicks=excluded.clicks, unique_clicks=excluded.unique_clicks`; aggregation unchanged. No other UPDATE against links in apps/worker. (4) apps/redirect/src/resolver.ts - ResolvedLink interface byte-for-byte unchanged; PostgresLinkResolver.resolve() adds .leftJoin(linkCounters, ...) and selects clicks via coalesce(linkCounters.clicks, 0), sets clicks: row.clicks. Imported linkCounters. gateFor unchanged. (5) apps/api/src/links/links.service.ts - list() count + paged queries and get() add LEFT JOIN link_counters; paged/get select coalesced clicks/uniqueClicks and spread onto LinkRow; the four raw-SQL status-filter references to ${links.clicks} replaced with coalesce(${linkCounters.clicks}, 0). exportCsv unchanged. links.mapper.ts LinkRow/DTO unchanged. (6) apps/api/src/conversions/conversions.service.ts - byLink selects coalesce(linkCounters.clicks,0), adds LEFT JOIN link_counters, groupBy uses linkCounters.clicks. (7) Tests: rollup.test.ts reads link_counters by link_id; links.service.integration.test.ts addLink() no longer sets clicks on links insert, inserts a link_counters row instead (imported linkCounters). Contract Link.clicks/uniqueClicks unchanged; web fixtures untouched. Verification: `pnpm type-check` PASS; `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL=... pnpm build` PASS; `pnpm test` PASS (DB-gated rollup.test.ts and links.service.integration.test.ts skip locally with no DATABASE_URL, as expected - they run in CI); `pnpm --filter @snapurl/database generate` reports no drift. grep confirms no remaining reader of links.clicks/unique_clicks and no UPDATE against links in scheduled jobs. FOLLOW-UP (issue #270 missed reader) COMPLETED: (a) apps/worker/src/jobs/outbox.ts sweepExpired() - added `left join link_counters lc on lc.link_id = l.id` and changed the click-limit predicate from `l.clicks >= l.click_limit` to `coalesce(lc.clicks, 0) >= l.click_limit`. The newly_expired CTE, projection_outbox insert, and count are otherwise unchanged; coalesce(...,0) matches the resolver's zero-default for links with no counter row. This was the scheduled job (invoked from apps/worker/src/main.ts:69) that would have thrown once migration 0009 dropped links.clicks. (b) Also fixed packages/database/scripts/seed.ts:150 which was the last remaining writer of the dropped links.clicks/unique_clicks columns (a dev seed script, not scheduled, but it would fail at runtime post-0009): replaced `update links l set clicks=..., unique_clicks=...` with `insert into link_counters (link_id, clicks, unique_clicks) select link_id, sum(clicks)::int, sum(uniques)::int from click_daily group by link_id on conflict (link_id) do update set ...`, mirroring the rollup upsert. Re-verified: pnpm type-check PASS, NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL=... pnpm build PASS, pnpm test PASS (DB-gated suites skip locally as expected), `pnpm --filter @snapurl/database generate` reports 'No schema changes, nothing to migrate' (no drift). grep confirms the only remaining links.clicks-style hits are DTO/service reads against link_counters (mapper row.uniqueClicks, links.service coalesced link_counters reads).
